statement: Micron committed $250 billion to US DRAM manufacturing through 2035, targeting 40% of total output domestically, and broke ground on its New York fab on July 9, 2026.
why: Very large multi-year memory capex is the mechanism by which today's shortage eventually resolves, but on a timeline measured in years, not quarters.

impact.mechanism: Committed fab capital and a started groundbreaking add future DRAM and HBM bit supply, easing the memory constraint on accelerator production over the long run.

evidence.excerpt: Micron has committed $250 billion in US DRAM manufacturing investment through 2035.
Micron US DRAM capacity target: 40% of total output domestically by 2035.

confidence.basis: Secondary open-web article; figures not verified against a primary Micron filing in this document.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: value 26.5 -> 250.0 (tol 1%); sources: Silicon Analysts
